sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Codename pattern and imports
sections.what: Brings in the test tool and defines the list of internal names and old product names that must not appear.
sections.why: Centralises the forbidden names so every check uses the same list.
sections.watch_out: The list is hard-coded, so renaming or adding an internal name requires editing this file.

sections.name: PUBLIC_PAGES
sections.title: Public pages and manifest checks
sections.what: Checks each public page's visible text, title and metadata for forbidden names and confirms the title contains ALTER EGO. It also checks the manifest's name is ALTER EGO and contains no forbidden names.
sections.why: Covers both what users see and what phones and search tools read.
sections.watch_out: Image alt text and meta content are checked, so a rename in those places also needs the same care.

summary: Browser tests that check internal project codenames and old product names do not appear on any public page, in page metadata, or in the web app manifest.
purpose: Keeps the public brand consistent as ALTER EGO and hides internal names from users.
why: Internal codenames should never reach users, and the public name must match everywhere.
how: For each public page, it loads the page, reads all visible text and the page title, meta tags and image alt text, and checks none match the codename pattern. It also checks the title contains ALTER EGO. A separate test fetches the manifest file and checks its name is ALTER EGO and that it contains no codename.
inputs: The public page paths and the manifest endpoint.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each page and for the manifest.
risks: A new codename or old name added to the list must also be added to the pattern, or it will not be caught.
debug: If a page fails, the reported text shows where the name appeared. Search the page template and metadata for that name.
